In summary, our research is concerned with
the production and emission of pyruvic acids and its volatile metabolite, which is an essential precursor to the biosynthesis of a variety of isoprenoid compounds.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pyruvic acid plays an important role as a substrate for the production of a wide variety of VOCs in tropical rainforests.
pyruvic acid plays a key role in the synthesis of many oxygenated VOCs and isoprenoids in TRF.

pyruvic acid serves as a source of carbon for isoprenoids, and that pyruvic and pyruvic acid-derived compounds are precursors to the oxygenated VOC acetaldehyde, acetic acid and acetone, but not ethanol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pyruvic acid can serve as a precursor to a large suite of biogenic VOCs, and that the PDH bypass system is an important pathway to the production of several of these VOCs.
the PDH bypass pathway is an important contributor to the production of isomers of pyruvic and other VOCs in the TRF biome.
the pyruvic acid pathway may be a significant contributor to isoprene, monoterpene, and sesqueterpene emissions from tropical plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pyruvic acid plays a central role in the biosynthesis of a wide array of VOCs in TRF.
pyruvic acid may be a more important precursor for VOCs than previously thought.
pyruvic acid may be a precursor to a large number of VOCs, including both isoprenoid and oxygenated compounds.
